files.s: We give the definition of the Frattini subgroup of a group, and three elementary results: * The Frattini subgroup is characteristic. * If every subgroup of a group is contained in a maximal subgroup, then the Frattini subgroup consists of the non-generating elements of the group. * The Frattini subgroup of a finite group is nilpotent.

h.d: When `G` is finite, the Frattini subgroup is nilpotent.

The Frattini subgroup consists of "non-generating" elements in the following sense: If a subgroup together with the Frattini subgroup generates the whole group, then the subgroup is already the whole group.
The Frattini subgroup of a group is the intersection of the maximal subgroups.
